card.name: Comma before monitoring instructions
card.fires_on: A comma or 'and' ending an opening condition clause in a warning, right before an instruction verb such as assess, monitor or follow. Also 'be' after 'should' before 'evaluated'.

modes.label: Comma after condition
modes.description: Comma closing an 'if/before/in patients with' clause, just ahead of an imperative like assess or monitor.
modes.example: Before initiating dapagliflozin in patients with one or more of these characteristics<<,>> assess volume status and renal function.

modes.label: 'and' joining instructions
modes.description: 'and' after a list of prescribing steps, just before 'follow patients closely'.
modes.example: prescribe the lowest effective dosages and minimum durations of concomitant use,<< and>> follow patients closely for signs and symptoms of

modes.label: Should be
modes.description: 'be' after 'should' just before a follow-up action such as evaluated.
modes.example: should<< be>> evaluated by an ophthalmologist.

card.writes: Little clear effect; it may favor words starting symptom-related terms like 'sympt', but the tokens are mixed.
card.plain: It fires at the point in a warning where the label turns from a condition to telling the clinician to monitor or assess.
